lessons: Never repeat the video title word-for-word as the hook line—repeating the prompt (e.g., in the Potato video) caused an immediate 31.8% viewer drop.
Avoid empty filler statements like 'They are not just there to look cool' or 'They look like similar fruits'; viewers leave instantly when explanation is delayed.
Do not include interactive pauses or countdowns ('Pause and guess'); both instances in the dataset triggered immediate drops in retention.

Hooks that state a mind-bending counter-intuitive fact or stark visual contrast (e.g., 'older than the United States' or 'tuna vs cod meat') yield over 1.0 retention at 10% and significantly outperform baseline.
Avoid line duplication or repeating concepts across consecutive sentences; duplicated lines in guardrail scripts caused repeated viewer exits.
worst_moment_types: Verbatim title repetition at the start of the video
Empty filler tease sentences that delay explaining the mechanism
Interactive pauses and explicit countdown prompts ('Pause and guess... three, two, one')
Repeating the exact same phrase or explanation line twice
best_hook_types: Extreme historical/scale contrast statements ('This shark is older than the United States')
Direct visual comparison between two common items ('A bluefin tuna and a cod are both fish, but their meat looks like two completely different animals')
Everyday counter-intuitive science facts ('You can touch hot foil briefly just as it comes out of the oven')
